newsitem.title: THAILAND: Decision on Thai exit from tin group awaited.
newsitem.headline: Decision on Thai exit from tin group awaited.

text.p: A final cabinet decision is awaited on Thailand's planned withdrawal from the Association of Tin Producing Countries (ATPC), a senior Industry Ministry official said on Tuesday.
Mondop Valayapetch, a metal specialist at the ministry, told Reuters he expected the ministry's decision for withdrawal to be approved by the government but declined to speculate on the timing.
He said the move to leave the Kuala Lumpur-based ATPC was prompted by the fact that Thailand had become a net importer of the metal.
During the first half of 1996, Thailand imported 4,184 tonnes of tin concentrates and produced only 758 tonnes, according to ministry data.
In 1995, the country imported 7,638 tonnes of concentrates and produced 1,783 tonnes domestically.
Thai miners produced less tin because many had been forced out of business by the gradual fall in prices, he added.
The price fall was caused by a lack of control in exports from producing countries outside ATPC, such as Brazil and Peru, he said.
Although the tin producers' group decided in June to scrap the export quota system, Thailand would not change its mind as the country had already become a net importer, he said.
Mondop noted the cabinet decision on any withdrawal might not be made in time for the upcoming ATPC meeting, to be held later this month in Singapore.
"We can just send a letter informing the group that we intend to leave later. This will take effect three months after the submission," he said.
ATPC members include Australia, Bolivia, China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand and Zaire.
